summary: Backend regression for BUG #1 (proxy-session freshness). Created pytest suite /app/backend/tests/test_proxy_session_refresh.py with 8 tests covering: admin login, proxy check-in of two colleagues via a lending phone, duplicate check-in 409, the CORE FIX (one /api/mobile/location from lender bumps last_live_ts_ms on BOTH proxied sessions), isolation (different user's fix does NOT refresh those proxy sessions), regression on own-session live-location update, and admin /api/sessions/live view showing both proxies fresh & not stale. All 8 tests PASS.
critical_code_review_comments: mobile.py update_many correctly filters by org_id + source='proxy_checkin' + proxy_by == user.email + status='active' — safe against cross-org leakage and paused sessions.

Note: the proxy update_many runs BEFORE the stale_replay watermark check. That's intentional (proxy sessions have their own watermark implicitly via last_live_ts_ms $set), but a very old replayed fix (offline batch) could still refresh proxy sessions to that older ts. Consider guarding update_many with `last_live_ts_ms: {$lt: now_ms}` to make offline replay idempotent for proxies too — minor edge case, not user-visible for the current live-stream path.

_sanitize_session does not expose last_live_ts_ms directly to admins; last_fix.ts_ms serves as the observable freshness proxy — acceptable but worth surfacing explicitly if the admin UI ever needs the exact watermark.

colleague/checkin sets last_live_ts_ms=now_ms at creation, so proxied sessions are 'fresh' immediately — the fix now keeps them fresh across subsequent location fixes from the lender. Verified end-to-end.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The regression file is reusable: /app/backend/tests/test_proxy_session_refresh.py. It handles the case where prior 'test_proxy_*' users exist (resets password + office + face baseline). If face_baseline check ever tightens (e.g. must be a real dlib embedding), the DB-seeding of [0.01]*128 will need to be replaced with a real enrolled face via POST /api/face/enroll. Also documented: _sanitize_session omits last_live_ts_ms; use last_fix.ts_ms as the admin-visible freshness signal.
rca of the issue: BUG #1 RCA — In /api/mobile/location the handler only refreshed last_live_ts_ms on the streaming user's OWN active_session (matched by user_id). Proxy sessions live under the ABSENT colleague's user_id with source='proxy_checkin' and proxy_by=<lender email>, so they never received a refresh from the lender's location stream and went stale (~STALE_PING_MS) → 'offline' in admin dashboard. Checking in a 2nd colleague on the same lending phone did NOT re-refresh the first. FIX (line ~579-585 of mobile.py) adds a db.active_sessions.update_many that sets last_live_ts_ms + last_fix on every active proxy_checkin session vouched by the streaming user's email. Verified: BEFORE emp_a/emp_b last_live_ts_ms == check-in time; after one location fix, BOTH are bumped to the fix's now_ms (strictly greater, and >= now_ms-500). Isolation verified: a different user's location fix leaves emp_a/emp_b unchanged. Own-session regression verified: streaming user's own session's last_live_ts_ms still advances. Duplicate check-in still 409.
